projects.title: AMED — Smart Contact Lens for Intraocular Pressure Monitoring
paragraphs: I prepared PEDOT:PSS and PEDOT:PSS/PVA multilayer cracked resistive films, including acid treatment and formulation optimization for sensitivity, response stability, and optical transmission.

I developed capacitive pressure sensors using wrinkled-gold electrodes and an Ecoflex dielectric layer. I carried out photolithography, gold evaporation, electroplating, and ultrathin flexible antenna fabrication, with HFSS simulation, VNA / LCR measurements, and MATLAB analysis.

I contributed to PT-symmetric wireless readout integration. In collaboration with Vizionfocus, I was responsible for sensor preparation and post-integration performance testing and validation; the company performed embedding and integration into hydrogel lenses.
projects.role: Core doctoral project · Research Assistant during the project

results.label: Resistive sensing
results.detail: Minimum visible-light transmittance of the sensing films: 82.8%. With PT-symmetric wireless readout: system-level IOP response sensitivity of 47.31 Ω/mmHg, approximately 15 times the conventional scheme. Correlation with reference IOP: R² = 0.93 in ex vivo porcine eyes and 0.97 in in vivo rabbit eyes.

results.label: Capacitive sensing
results.detail: Capacitance response sensitivity increased from 393 to 1057 ppm/mmHg compared with planar gold electrodes. Electrode resistance remained essentially stable at approximately 50% stretch. With PT-symmetric wireless readout, detection sensitivity improved by approximately 7.5 times relative to the conventional system.

projects.title: Moonshot Research Project — Contact Lens Biosensor Development
paragraphs: I participate in the development of new contact lens biosensors, taking responsibility for flexible sensing-element preparation, device processing, and prototype performance evaluation.

As part of the team exploring eye-movement recognition with wireless smart contact lenses, I conduct performance tests, collect and analyze experimental data, and evaluate device sensing responses. This work is ongoing.

projects.title: Stretchable Gold Antenna Fabrication & Contact Lens Integration
paragraphs: I fabricated one- to three-turn horseshoe-shaped stretchable gold antennas on ITO conductive substrates, with approximately 25 μm linewidth and 7 μm gold thickness, to provide antenna devices for subsequent hydrogel contact lens integration.

Using EDOT electrochemical polymerization, I formed a PEDOT electrochemical adhesion layer and integrated gold antennas onto hydrogel contact lens surfaces. The devices remained attached under stretching and 180° twisting, with no obvious degradation of resonance characteristics after bonding.

I analyzed gold-electroplating experimental data, fabricated antennas, reported progress, and exchanged technical findings with the Japanese industry partner to support process development and prototype validation.
projects.role: Industry collaboration · Kojima Chemicals Co., Ltd. (小島化学薬品株式会社), Japan
